Hence p=1/2 is necessary. On that line write local transition as exp[b t_i(s_{i-1}+s_{i+1})]/(2 cosh[b(s_{i-1}+s_{i+1})]), b=atanh(2r-1)/2; multiplying the product kernel by W(s)=∏2cosh[b(s_{i-1}+s_{i+1})] makes a symmetric bilinear two-time exponent, proving detailed balance and uniqueness. Expanding W gives J=-log(4r(1-r))/4 coupled sites distance two. The graph splits into two disjoint length N/2 cycles for even N and one length N for odd N. The Ising transfer matrix eigenvalues 2cosh J,2sinh J yield C_k=(q^k+q^(m-k))/(1+q^m), susceptibility, strict even/odd independence and nearest-neighbor zero on even N. With N sqrt(1-r)->xi for odd sizes, q^N->exp(-4xi), giving sech(2xi). Finite N checks are corroboration, not universal proof; degeneracies r=1/2 and N=3 handled by the same algebra.
